item.title: Cop takes on AI judge in sci-fi thriller
item.description: Set in the near future, “Mercy” paints a grim vision of the use and influence of artificial intelligence in society. Source: Australian Catholics.

item.title: Norwegian Trappist to preach papal Lenten retreat
item.description: Pope Leo XIV has chosen Norwegian Trappist Bishop Erik Varden to preach the first papal Lenten retreat of his pontificate with the Roman Curia later this month. Source: OSV News.

item.title: Ukraine prelate says faith endures four years after invasion
item.description: Nearly four years after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, faith remains central to Ukraine’s endurance, the country’s prelate says. Source: NCR Online.

item.title: Preschool for three-year-olds get kids off to a flying start
item.description: The start of the new school year marks an exciting milestone for Catholic Education South Australia, with six schools welcoming their youngest learners through the rollout of a preschool program for three-year-olds.

item.title: ACRATH calls community to anti-slavery prayer pilgrimage
item.description: This International Day of Prayer and Awareness Against Human Trafficking, Australian Catholic Religious Against Trafficking in Humans (ACRATH) is inviting people to join a global movement of prayer, reflection and action. Source: Melbourne Catholic.

item.title: National survey finds one in four older Australian living in poverty
item.description: Huge inequity exists within the older generation of Australians, says former Liberal minister Christopher Pyne, now Chair of Council on the Ageing. Source: The Weekly Source.

item.title: Auxiliary Bishop-elect plans to be a ‘shepherd who listens’
item.description: Perth Auxiliary Bishop-elect Nelson Po has a simple and pastoral vision for the kind of bishop he hopes to be after his episcopal ordination. Source: The Record.

item.title: World falling short of protecting and caring for its children: Pope
item.description: The world continues to fall short of protecting and caring for its children, leaving them with few opportunities to succeed and at greater risk of suffering abuse, Pope Leo XIV said yesterday. Source: CNS.

item.title: An invitation to reflect on those who live with illness
item.description: Catholics are being urged to reflect during this year’s World Day of the Sick on February 11. Source: ACBC Media Blog.
